source_text:
Περὶ δὲ τοῦ βαπτίσματος, οὕτω βαπτίσατε: ταῦτα πάντα προειπόντες, βαπτίσατε εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἐν ὕδατι ζῶντι.
ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἔχῃς ὕδωρ ζῶν, εἰς ἄλλο ὕδωρ βάπτισον: εἰ δ’ οὐ δύνασαι ἐν ψυχρῷ, ἐν θερμῷ.
ἐὰν δὲ ἀμφότερα μὴ ἔχῃς, ἔκχεον εἰς τὴν κεφαλὴν τρὶς ὕδωρ εἰς ὄνομα πατρὸς καὶ υἱοῦ καὶ ἁγίου πνεύματος.
πρὸ δὲ τοῦ βαπτίσματος προνηστευσάτω ὁ βαπτίζων καὶ ὁ βαπτιζόμενος καὶ εἴ τινες ἄλλοι δύνανται: κελεύεις δὲ νηστεῦσαι τὸν βαπτιζόμενον πρὸ μιᾶς ἢ δύο.
orientation: The anonymous author is giving the community its instructions for performing baptism, after finishing the moral teaching of the Two Ways.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning but the baptism, thus baptize: these things all [after] saying beforehand, baptize into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit in water living. If but not you have water living, into other water baptize; if but not you are able in cold, in warm. If but both not you have, pour out onto the head three times water into [the] name of Father and of Son and of Holy Spirit. Before but the baptism let fast beforehand the [one] baptizing and the [one] being baptized and if any others are able; you command but to fast the [one] being baptized before one or two [days].

choices.why: The glossary does not cover this phrase, but 'living water' is the standard literal rendering of the Greek and preserves the distinction from standing or stored water.

choices.english: after saying all these things beforehand
choices.why: The participle is aorist and refers to the preceding moral teaching; 'beforehand' preserves the temporal force of προ-.
The present indicative second-person singular is used as an instruction to the person baptizing; rendering it as an obligation keeps the directive force.

choices.english: for one or two days beforehand
choices.why: The numeral is feminine singular, implying 'day' (ἡμέρα) is understood; supplying 'days' makes the sense clear in English.

bible_refs.note: εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος

pass_b_english: Now about baptism, this is how you are to baptize: after saying all these things beforehand, baptize in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit in living water.
If you do not have living water, baptize in other water; and if you cannot do it in cold water, use warm.
If you have neither, pour water on the head three times in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
Before the baptism, the one baptizing and the one being baptized are to fast beforehand, and any others who are able. You are to command the one being baptized to fast for one or two days beforehand.

last_rejected.why: 'warm' alone omits 'water'; Greek ἐν θερμῷ means 'in warm [water]', parallel to 'in cold [water]'
last_rejected.ruling: Context supplies 'water'; 'use warm' elliptically renders ἐν θερμῷ correctly, parallel to 'in cold'.

last_rejected.quote: for one or two days beforehand
last_rejected.why: English adds 'days' not in source; Greek says 'before one or two' without specifying days
last_rejected.fix: to fast beforehand for one or two [days]
last_rejected.ruling: πρὸ μιᾶς ἢ δύο with fasting context idiomatically means 'one or two days'; 'days' is implied, not added.
